# The FIRST Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft Of The Year - Jokic Or Wemby At 1?

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-08-11, 51:01. https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc

## Summary

Josh Lloyd does the first 9-category head-to-head mock draft of the season: 12 teams, 14 roster spots, third round reversal. He picks second. Jokic goes first and he takes Wembanyama. His team ends up as Wembanyama, Anthony Davis, Jaylen Brown, Dejounte Murray, Matas Buzelis, Pascal Siakam, Coby White, Immanuel Quickley, Jusuf Nurkic, Shaedon Sharpe, CJ McCollum, Paul Reed, Jeremiah Fears and Jimmy Butler. He comments on value as the picks come in. He thinks Cooper Flagg, Clingan, Derrick White, Dylan Harper and Pritchard went too early. He sees Giannis at 8, Trey Murphy and Trae Young as good value. He is low on Jalen Johnson, Haliburton, Fox and Brunson. His strategy points: draft for value instead of locking into a punt early, take upside flyers from round 10 on, and treat injury-risk veterans differently in head-to-head than in roto. He says picking Quickley over Kevin Porter Jr. was a mistake.

## Rules and methods

- [1:50](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=110) The mock league format is 9-category, 12 teams, 14 roster spots, 10 starters, 4 bench, with a third round reversal.
  > "It's a nine category league. 12 teams, 14 roster spots, 10 starters, four bench, third round reversal."
- [8:26](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=506) Low-scoring players are harder to build around unless you are comfortable punting points.
  > "the low scoring can be harder to build around unless you're very comfortable just punting that category"
- [8:39](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=519) He avoids stacking old players with repeated lower body injuries early in the draft.
  > "So that's a lot of old and a lot of injury, just repeated lower body stuff, which is not what I love to do."
- [11:54](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=714) Free throws are the most variable fantasy category. Draft a poor shooter expecting bad free throws, so any improvement is a bonus.
  > "We know that free throws are the most highly variable fantasy category, but if it you at least go in"
- [13:49](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=829) A straight 9-cat ranking can be misleading. He uses other measures to judge value.
  > "if you look at a straight NAT ranking, it's going to tell you some stuff that is um not super accurate"
- [17:05](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1025) Players coming off a long Finals run often start slow, with production dips and fatigue.
  > "He's off a finals run. So the these guys often start slow and can see some of their production dip"
- [21:18](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1278) Drafting injury-prone stars like Kawhi and Embiid worked in a large roto league, but head-to-head is a lot different.
  > "by drafting Kawawaii and Embiid in that in that league. So it was Roto and it worked fine for me."
- [22:56](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1376) People overindex on punting. Punting wins leagues, but early in the draft focus on value and lean into a punt later if one appears.
  > "People overindex on punting a lot. I I believe punting is a strong thing. It's a very good thing"
- [36:30](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=2190) Take upside flyers from round 10 on. Leagues are won by players who beat their draft slot by a lot. A safe pick that finishes at his draft slot means nothing.
  > "you get a guy at 100 and he's the 40th best player. You you you're there."
- [36:41](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=2201) Don't play it safe in round 10. Go for upside.
  > "If you get a guy at 100 and he ends up 100th, it means nothing. So don't go safe in round 10"
- [49:44](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=2984) An injured star is fine as a last-round pick to stash in an IL spot. Drop him for a waiver player if the IL spots fill up.
  > "I don't hate him as a last round pick because my last round guy you he goes in my I'll add someone off waiverss"
- [26:07](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1567) A backup big with strong per-minute production behind a starter is worth drafting because he becomes valuable if the starter misses time.
  > "if Duran misses time, Paul Reed's going to be a top 50 player. He's definitely he definitely has to be"
